Frequently Asked Questions

Got Questions? We Have Answers

Everything you need to know about our visiting charges, appointment scheduling, spare parts warranty, and diagnostic process.

Under standard conditions, our technician can reach your doorstep within 60 to 90 minutes of booking confirmation, depending on your locality and the time of day. You can also schedule an appointment for a preferred date and time slot.

A visiting or inspection fee starts from ₹199 depending on the appliance. If you go ahead with the repair, the visiting charge is adjusted in the final repair invoice. The estimate is always shared for approval before work starts.

Eligible repair work may include a 30-day service warranty. Coverage, exclusions and claim requirements depend on the written warranty terms shared for the service.

No. Service Support Hub is an independent multi-brand service provider. Brand names are used only to identify the appliances we can help with, and we are not affiliated with or authorised by any manufacturer unless stated in writing.

The most common culprit is heavy grease clogging the baffle or mesh filters, or oil coating the blower fan blades. In auto-clean chimneys a faulty heating coil can stop the oil from draining. A deep clean or duct unblocking normally restores suction.

A yellow flame indicates incomplete combustion. It is usually caused by clogged burner ports or jets, spills blocking the air intake, or low or unsteady regulator pressure. Cleaning and re-setting the burner restores a clean blue flame.

Continuous clicking usually points to moisture or food residue at the spark plug or a jammed ignition switch. It rarely causes immediate danger, but switch off the electrical supply and the gas knob and book a visit to avoid damaging the pulse generator.

This usually indicates a failed magnetron, a blown high-voltage diode or capacitor, or a faulty transformer. These parts carry high voltage, so please do not open the oven yourself.

Typical reasons are a failing compressor or start relay, a faulty thermostat or sensor, an evaporator fan that has stopped, a frost-blocked coil, or a gas leak. Cooling in the freezer but not in the fridge section often points to a fan, damper or defrost problem.

Common causes are an unbalanced or overloaded drum, a worn belt or motor coupler, a faulty lid or door lock switch, a motor or capacitor problem, or a PCB fault. The technician checks these before suggesting any part.

Common causes are dirty filters or coils, low refrigerant because of a leak, a weak compressor or capacitor, a faulty sensor, or a blocked outdoor unit. A technician checks airflow, pressure and electrical parts first, and shares the estimate before any repair.

Sound with a black screen usually points to a failed backlight (LED strip or driver) or a main-board or T-con fault. Shine a torch at the screen at an angle; a faint image confirms a backlight problem.

A burnt heating element, a faulty thermostat or thermal cut-out, a power-supply problem or heavy scale build-up are the usual reasons. The technician tests each of them before recommending a part.

Choked sediment or carbon filters, a weak pump, a clogged membrane or low inlet pressure are the common causes. Filters usually need replacement every 6 to 12 months depending on water quality.

Power supply (SMPS) failure, loose or corroded BNC/RJ45 connectors, damaged cable or a faulty camera or DVR/NVR port are the usual causes. The technician checks them one by one.

A blocked filter, kinked or clogged drain hose, or a failed drain pump are the usual causes. Clean the filter as per the manual and book a visit if water remains.
